la:verb:paeniteo.gloss: to cause (someone) to regret or repent
senses: to cause (someone) to regret or repent
to regret, repent; to be sorry
la:verb:paeniteo.html:
paenĭtĕo (less correctly poen-), ui, no
sup., ēre, 2, v. a. and impers. [root in poena, q. v.; Gr. ποινή].
Pers.
Act., to cause to repent, to displease (anteclass. and late Lat.): et me quidem haec conditio nunc non paenitet,causes me no regret,: quod male emptum est semper paenitet, Cat. ap. : paenitemini et credite Evangelio,repent,; .—
Neutr., to repent, be sorry: momenta certaminum assuefaciebant militem minus jam tandem aut virtutis aut fortunae paenitere suae,: etiam nunc paenitere suā sponte Aequos quam pati hostilia malle,: Athenienses primi paenitere coeperunt,: paenituit populus,: non vult paenitere,.—Esp., in part. pres.: Lepidus paenitens consili, Dietsch: paenitens facti,; cf. ; cf. II. A. ε and ι infra.—
Impers.
It repents one, etc., i. e. I, you, etc., repent; I, etc., repent, am sorry, grieve, rue, etc.
Aliquem alicujus rei: non paenitere me consilii de tuā mansione,: quem ... in eam diem vitae non paenituerat,: neque te, neque quenquam arbitror tuae paeniturum laudis, App. ap. : galeatum sero duelli paenitet, .—
Alicujus rei alone: bonae mentis paenituisset,, praef. 7: paenitebatque modo consilii, modo paenitentiae ipsius,.—
Aliquem alone: si eos quidem non paeniteret,.—
With acc. of person, foll. by inf.: efficiunt ut me non didicisse minus paeniteat,.—(ε) With neutr. pron. as subj. (cf. I. B. supra; Zumpt, Gr. § 442, explains the pron. in these passages as acc., but v. Krebs, Antibarb. p. 876): sapientis est nihil, quod paenitere possit, facere,: sequitur ut nihil paeniteat,: quaeri oportet utrum id facinus sit, quod paenitere fuerit necesse,. —(ζ) Foll. by rel. adverb. clause: etsi solet eum, cum aliquid fecit, paenitere,.—(η) With quod: valde ego ipsi, quod de suā sententiā decesserit, paenitendum puto,: paenitet quod non ab adultero coepi,.— (θ) With dat. of agent: consilii nostri ... nobis paenitendum,.—(ι) Absol.: tanta vis fuit paenitendi,: corrigere errorem paenitendo, id. Fragm. ap. : Sallustius usque eo processit, ut non paeniturum pro non acturo paenitentiam dixerit,: paenitet et torqueor,; .—
It discontents or displeases one, i. e. one is vexed, angry, offended, dissatisfied (class.; cf. taedet).
Aliquem alicujus rei: ut me imperii nostri paeniteret,: num hujusce te gloriae paenitebat?; cf. : num igitur, si ad centesimum annum vixisset, senectutis suae eum paeniteret?: paenitere se virium suarum,: paenituit multos vanae sterilisque cathedrae,.—
With quod and subj.: se paenitere, quod animum tuum offenderit,.—
It concerns, is a care to, makes anxious, dissatisfies; and with negative, it is enough, satisfies (mostly anteclass.): an paenitet te, quanto hic fuerit usui?are you not satisfied?: paenitetne te, quot ancillas alam?: duas dabo, una si parum'st; et si duarum paenitebit, addentur duae,are not enough, not satisfactory,: an paenitebat flagitii te auctore quod fecisset Adulescens?was it not enough?; ; : an paenitet vos, quod salvum atque incolumem exercitum traduxerim?: quod a senatu quanti fiam minime me paenitet,; cf.: tam diu velle debebis (discere), quoad te quantum proficias non paenitebit,. —Hence,
paenĭtens, entis, P. a., repenting, repentant, penitent.
Absol.: optimus est portus paenitenti mutatio consilii,.—
With gen.: Lepidum paenitentem consilii, Sall. ap. P.—
With de: signa paenitentis de matrimonio dederat,.— Hence, adv.: paenĭtenter, with regret, repentantly (late Lat.): auguria paenitenter omissa,.—
paenĭ-tendus, a, um, to be repented of, blamable, objectionable (perh. not ante-Aug.).
Affirmatively: itaque hic ager sive exercetur, seu cessat, colono est paenitendus,: paenitendae rei recordatio,.—
With a negative: sub haud paenitendo magistro,; ; : dicta non paenitenda,: gens Flavia reipublicae non paenitenda,.

la:noun:paedagogus.html:
paedăgōgus, i, m., = παιδαγωγός, lit.
a slave who took the children to school and had the charge of them at home, a governor, preceptor, pedagogue (cf. praeceptor).
Lit.: non paedagogum jam me, sed Ludum vocat,: nutrices et paedagogi,: tamquam quicquam aliud sit sapiens quam humani generis paedagogus,: de paedagogis hoc amplius, ut aut sint eruditi plane, aut se non esse eruditos sciant,; cf. ; ; ; 1, 3, 15; 6, 1, 41 et saep.—Terence jestingly gives the name paedagogus to a young man who accompanied his sweetheart to and from school. .—
Adj.: lex paedagoga, (cf.: lex paedagogus,). —
Transf.
In gen., a leader, guide, : unicuique nostrum paedagogum dari deum inferioris notae,; cf. ; . —
A pedant: hic dux, hic ille est paedagogus,; cf. .

la:adv:paene.html:
paene (less correctly pēne), adv.
etym. dub.
,
nearly, almost, as I may say (class.): fores paene effregisti,; ; ; : aliquem paene perdere,: paene amicus,: paene communis,: Brutum non minus amo, quam tu: paene dixi quam te,; : non solum in omnibus civitatibus, sed paene etiam in singulis domibus, factiones sunt,: quam paene furvae regna Proserpinae ... vidimus,: paene manu, quod amo, tanta est vicinia, tango: Saepe sed, heu! lacrimas hoc mihi paene movet,.—Rarely with subj.: nisi nostri equites acutius vidissent, paene concedente adversario superasset,: legiones duas paene delessent, ni, etc.,.—Paene sometimes follows the word it qualifies: omnibus par paene laus tribuitur,: totidem paene reperiantur genera,: cuncta paene,; 3, 55, 209: divini paene est viri,; ; ; : et crescere paene opus,; ; ; 4, 27, 11: nudā paene cathedrā,.— Sup.: ita mea consilia perturbat paenissume (penissime),utterly, completely,: me paenissume perdidit,: paenissime os alicui sublinere,; ; ; cf. and 1008 P.

la:noun:paenula.gloss: A kind of sleeveless cloak or mantle with an opening for the head, worn on journeys or in rainy weather.
senses: A kind of sleeveless cloak or mantle with an opening for the head, worn on journeys or in rainy weather.
la:noun:paenula.html:
paenŭla (pēn-), ae, f.,
a woollen outer garment covering the whole body, a kind of cloak or mantle, worn on journeys, and also in the city in rainy weather (cf.: laena, lacerna): paenulam in caput induce, ne te noscat, Pompon. ap. ; so Lucil. ib.: paenulā irretitus,: incolumi Rhodos ... facit quod Paenula solstitio,; : non quaerenda est homini, qui habet virtutem, paenula in imbri, Varr. ap. : et multo stillaret paenula nimbo, ; cf. Varr. ap. Non. l. l.: paenulis intra Urbem frigoris causā ut senes uterentur, permisit ... matronas tamen intra Urbem paenulis uti vetuit,; .—In later times also worn by orators, .—Prov.: paenulam alicui scindere, i. e. to press one strongly to stay (opp.: vix paenulam alicui attingere),.—
Transf., a covering, cover, envelope, protection, Varr. ap. : libertas paenulast tergo tuo, Lorenz: ne paenula desit olivis,: supra catinum paenula, ut infundibulum inversum, est attemperata,.

la:adj:paetus.gloss: Having a cast in the eyes; blinking, winking or squinting with the eyes.
senses: Having a cast in the eyes; blinking, winking or squinting with the eyes.
la:adj:paetus.html:
paetus, a, um, adj.
etym. dub.
,
having leering eyes, with a cast in the eyes, blinking or winking with the eyes, blinkeyed; esp. as an epithet of Venus, prettily leering, with a pretty cast in her eyes, prettily

blinking

: paetus, μύωψ τοῖς ὄμμασιν, Gloss. Philox.: uni animalium homini depravantur oculi: unde Strabonum et Paetorum cognomina,; Plaut. Fragm. ap. Fest. s. v. valgos, p. 375 Müll.: strabonem Appellat paetum pater,.—Of Venus: non haec res de Venere paeta strabam facit? Varr. ap. P.: si paeta est, Veneri similis,: Minerva flavo lumine est, Venus paeto,.

senses: of or belonging to Paeonia, Paeonian
la:adj:Paeonius.html:
Paeōnĭus, a, um, adj., = Παιώνιος,
of or belonging to the god of medicine (Παιών), healing, medicinal (poet.): herbae,: ope Paeoniā,: fontes,: unda,: cura,.

la:noun:paeonia.html:
paeōnĭa, ae, f., = παιωνία,
the peony, so named after its discoverer, Pæon, .

la:verb:paenitendus.gloss: which is to be regretted, which is to be repented
senses: which is to be regretted, which is to be repented

la:noun:paenitentia.html:
paenĭtentĭa, ae, f.
paeniteo
,
repentance, penitence (not in Cic.; cf. ).—Absol.: celerem paenitentiam sequi,: nec poenā commilitonum exterriti, nec paenitentiā conversi,: fidelissimus est ad honesta ex paenitentiā transitus,, praef. 3.—Plur.: serae dant poenas turpes paenitentiae,.—With gen.: coepti,: dicti,: gestae rei,; : paenitentiam agere, to repent: eo usque processum est, ut non paeniturum pro non acturo paenitentiam dixerit (Sallustius),: ejus (facinoris),; ; ; ;

la:verb:paedagogo.html:
paedăgōgo, āre, v. a.
paedagogus
,
to educate, instruct (ante- and post-class.): depulsum mammā paedagogandum accipit, Pac. ap. Fest. s. v. repotia, p. 281 Müll.; Fulg. Planc. Contin. Virg. fin.

la:noun:paedor.html:
paedor, ōris, m.
root pu-; Sanscr. pūje, to be rotten, stink; Gr. πύθομαι, πύον; cf. pus, puter, etc.
,
nastiness, filth (syn.: illuvies, sordes).
Lit.: barba paedore horrida, Poët. ap. : membra horrida paedore,; plur., : exuere paedorem,: longus in carcere paedor,; .—
Transf., a stink, stench (post-class.): sine paedore, , 14, 24.

la:adj:paenultimus.html:
paenultĭmus (pēn-), a, um, adj.
paene-ultimus
,
the last but one (post-class. for proximus a postremo, ): paenultima meta November,.—
Subst.: pae-nultĭma, ae, f. (sc. syllaba), the penultimate syllable, the penult: paenultimam circumflectere,.

la:adj:paetulus.gloss: Having a slight cast in the eyes; blinking, winking or squinting slightly.
senses: Having a slight cast in the eyes; blinking, winking or squinting slightly.
la:adj:paetulus.html:
paetŭlus, a, um,
adj. dim. [paetus], having a slight cast in the eye, slightly blinkeyed: redeo ad deos: ecquos si non tam strabones, at paetulos esse arbitramur?; cf. paetus.

senses: Hymn or song of victory or praise.
la:noun:paean.html:
Paean, ānis, m., = Παιάν.
An appellation of Apollo, as the healing deity: signum Paeanis,: Paeana voca,; ; cf. Müll.; .—
Transf.
A religious hymn, orig. in honor of Apollo, but also transf. to other deities, a festive hymn, hymn of triumph or praise, a pœan: conclamant socii laetum paeana secuti,; : Herculeum paeana canunt,: paeanem citare,.—As a simple exclamation, like hymenaee: dicite io Paean, et io bis dicite Paean,shout huzza!.—
The prevailing foot in the versification of such hymns, consisting of one long syllable and three short ones, and 218 (commonly written paeon, q. v.).

la:noun:paelex.gloss: concubine of a married man, mistress
senses: concubine of a married man, mistress
la:noun:paelex.html:
paelex (pēlex, and, only in inscriptions, pellex), icis, f.
akin to Sanscr. pallavaka, girl; Gr. παλλακίς, concubine
,
a kept mistress, concubine of a married man.
Lit.: antiqui proprie eam pelicem nominabant, quae uxorem habenti nubebat. Cui generi mulierum etiam poena constituta est a Numā Pompilio hāc lege: paelex aram Junonis ne tangito, etc., Paul. ex Müll.; cf. : libro Memorialium Masurius scribit: pelicem apud antiquos eam habitam, quae, cum uxor non esset, cum aliquo tamen vivebat eamque nunc vero nomine amicam, paulo honestiore concubinam appellari,; ; et saep.—With gen. of the wronged wife: filiae paelex,; : tune eris et matris paelex et adultera patris?: illa Jovis magni paelex, metuenda sorori,: fugit (Medea) ulta paelicem, Magni Creontis filiam,: horrida,.— Poet., of the cows, as rivals of Pasiphaë, who had become enamoured of a bull, .—
Transf.
A kept mistress, concubine, in gen. (post-class.): virginem constupratam servo suo paelicem dederat,: Artaxerxi regi Persarum ex paelicibus centum et quindecim filii fuere,; cf.: Granius Flaccus scribit, pelicem quosdam vocare eam, quae uxoris loco sine nuptiis in domo sit. .—
A male prostitute (postclass.), Paul. ex Müll.: Dolabella eum (Caesarem) pelicem reginae (appellavit), as the favorite of King Nicomedes,; in apposition, pelices ministri,.—*
Comically,

a substitute: quoties pelex culcita facta mea est (sc. matellae),.
la:noun:paelex.inflection: and, only in inscriptions, icis, f.
